newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil says natgas prices boost Q2.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil says natgas prices boost Q2.

text.p: Pennzoil Co said that higher natural gas prices in the second quarter of 1997 compared with a year ago and lower general and administrative expenses partly offset lower hydrocarbon production, higher depreciation and operating expenses.
Pennzoil reported that net income per share fell to $0.51 from $0.53 a year ago and that excluding one time charges, recurring net income was $0.76 per share compared with $0.54 per share a year ago.
Average natural gas prices rose to $1.98 per thousand cubic feet (mcf) from $1.83 a year ago. Crude oil prices rose to $15.66 per barrel from $15.51 in the year earlier period.

Hydrocarbon production declined by 4,200 barrels of oil equivalent (boe) year on year due to the sale of 11,200 boe of Canadian assets, but this was partly offset by new wells wells on the West Cameron 580 block in the Gulf of Mexico.
Production in the quarter was 62,781 barrels of crude per day, down from 65,009 barrels and natgas output was 616,360 mcfd, down from 628,472.

Pennzoil said that during the second quarter it was the successful bidder for blocks B2X-68/79 and B2X-70/80 in Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela and it will sign operating agreements later today. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
